findings.rationale: MN is an outlier on every screen. Its uploaded updates are anti-aligned with the median (mean_cos -0.55, min_cos -0.91) and its norm is about 3.5x the median. Its local discrimination is poor (AUC 0.643, pooled 0.805, z=-5.3). Its CITL is strongly negative (-0.077, z=-5.3): observed prevalence 0.200 vs mean predicted 0.124. Its O/E ratio is about 1.6 in both sex subgroups, so the outcome is over-recorded relative to the features, consistent with flipped labels rather than a subgroup-specific effect. The persistent negative CITL in the per-round drift table (rounds 4-20) points to a fault present from early on, so onset is set to round 1, though the per-round onset is not precisely resolved.

VT shows the same pattern as MN. Updates point against the median (mean_cos -0.44, min_cos -0.79) with a norm about 2x the median. Local AUC is the lowest in the federation (0.634, z=-5.3). CITL is negative (-0.062, z=-4.3) and observed prevalence (0.184) exceeds mean predicted risk (0.122). O/E ratios are about 1.3-1.6 across both sex groups, and an AgeGroup 4 subgroup shows O/E of about 18.8. This is consistent with flipped outcome labels. Onset is set to round 1 because the negative CITL is present across most rounds in the drift table.

CT has the same signature, though somewhat weaker. Updates are anti-aligned with the median (mean_cos -0.49, min_cos -0.83) and the median norm is about 2.2x the median. Local AUC is low (0.659, z=-4.6) and CITL is negative (-0.058, z=-4.1), with observed prevalence (0.188) above mean predicted risk (0.129). O/E is about 1.6 in sex 0 and 1.4 in sex 1. The per-round CITL for CT is noisier, with a clearer negative trend from about round 9 onward, so the onset is uncertain. Onset is recorded as round 1 with reduced confidence.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients using updates, performance, drift, feature-tail and subgroup views. Three clients (MN, VT, CT) stand apart consistently. Each has anti-aligned updates with inflated norms, low local AUC (0.63-0.66 vs pooled 0.805) and negative CITL with observed prevalence above predicted risk. Subgroup O/E ratios are elevated across both sexes, so the pattern is over-recorded outcomes rather than subgroup under-diagnosis. I read this as label_noise, not poisoning, because the local data and performance are anomalous too. Onset is uncertain: the per-round tables did not resolve it precisely, so round 1 is recorded for all three. CT is the least certain. No drift, missing-artefact, free-rider or explanation-instability findings were supported after noise adjustment: the drift flags were empty and the tail-percentile outliers were from small clients with z_noise under about 4.9. Budget was exhausted (0 left), so explanation-instability (attribution_churn) was not checked.
